Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

cd2030.core 1.4.3

  • Requires datasuite.ui 0.5.2: the Reports page lists the dataset’s reports and the standard reports again, and the builder has its kinds of chart, its themes, years and regions. Since datasuite.ui 0.5.0 the page said “No reports yet” over a dataset that has reports, and often showed no standard reports.

cd2030.core 1.4.2

  • National Coverage & Continuum: the heat map of the regions is drawn. Since 1.4.0 it showed “subscript out of bounds” in the app, for every dataset: the numbers on its tiles were coloured through a scale that has no legend, and the app, listing the chart’s legend for the customize panel, failed on it. The numbers are coloured without a scale, so it is drawn on any datasuite.ui (0.5.1 fixes the listing itself).
  • National Inequality and Sub-National Inequality with no region chosen: the chart is drawn. In 1.4.1 it showed “The size of nm (2) must be compatible with the size of x (3)”: the page gives the label of a region only when one is chosen, and the missing label left the colours one name short.
  • Reporting Rate: the heat map writes each number in the colour that reads on its tile, as the other heat maps do (it was black on all three colours).
  • Data Missingness: the charts for one indicator (“missing indicators by region”, the trend) say “Select an indicator to see this chart” when every indicator is chosen; the loader turned for ever. And the heat map’s card becomes small again when one indicator is chosen (datasuite.ui 0.5.1, now required).
  • The bar charts with a panel a region (reporting rate, outliers by region and by indicator, missing indicators by region) are as tall as their rows of panels need (datasuite.ui 0.5.1).
  • Denominator Selection: the National Coverage card shows its loader while the coverage is worked out. It was blank.
  • set_k_factors() on a dataset that has stored adjustment settings (one adjusted on the Data Adjustment page) changes the k in those settings too: they are what adjust_data() reads, and the new k was not used.
  • Internal Consistency: no deprecation warnings (cur_data(), size for a line), and the labels RMNCAH asked for and did not have (opv1_opv3, opt_instdeliveries) are translated.

cd2030.core 1.4.1

  • Bayesian Analysis no longer holds the app while a model is fitted. 1.4.0 asked for one background worker, and a plan of one worker is run in the app’s own process: every page waited for the whole fit (10 to 13 seconds for a national model, minutes for a sub-national one). The worker is now a separate process whatever their number; starting a fit gives the app back in 0.2 seconds.
  • Public/Private Share: the C-section bars are each country’s own. A sector’s share of the C-sections was taken from all the countries in the file together, so a country’s two bars added up to a fraction of its rate (Kenya 2022: 1.8 %, for a survey rate of 16.5 %). The built-in shares are corrected for the 32 countries, national and by area (data-raw/private_share_csection.R says how); the private share itself, the ratio of the two bars, was right and is unchanged. load_private_sector_data() takes the share within each country and year.
  • Sub-national Bayesian Analysis has a region and a year to choose.
    • One region: its estimates over the years, the chart the national page has for the country, with the country’s facility-data coverage beside the region’s.
    • Every region: the regions compared in the year chosen (it was always 2025), each with its model estimate and interval and its facility-data value, and the country’s facility-data value as a line. The year starts at the latest one the facility data has.
    • Facility-data values are with the indicator’s denominator, as the model’s are.
    • In R: plot() of a sub-national model takes year, national and legend_labels; cache$bayes_national_routine() gives the country’s values.
  • Sub-National Inequality with a region chosen shows the region’s own coverage beside its districts’ and the national coverage. It showed the national value under the region’s name (“Central Coverage”). plot() of such a table draws region_value when the table has it; legend_labels takes region.
  • The tables read as one family.
    • The three formatted tables (overall data quality score, service utilization data quality, national health system) have one look: the same header, section rows, lines, alignment and text. A cell judged against the threshold has the charts’ red, amber and green, with its number readable on each. They had three different section colours, their own borders, and “seagreen”, “yellow” and “red”.
    • The data tables of the pages (units with low reporting, with extreme outliers, with missing data, the adjustment’s changes by year, the units meeting a target) have the same options (compact rows, paged in tens when there are more than ten) and write numbers the same way: a count whole with its thousands apart (“12,345”), a rate or a coverage to one decimal, a year as it is.

cd2030.core 1.4.0

  • A change of setting writes the dataset’s file once. Each table a change cleared was a write of the whole file, so a new performance threshold (14 tables) took 1.7 seconds before the page could answer, a new denominator 0.7. In a running app the writes of one change are now gathered into one, made a moment after the page has its answer: the change itself takes no measurable time, the write about 0.1 second. An app that closes with a write waiting makes it; outside an app (a script, a test) the file is written at once, as before.

  • A setting clears the tables it enters, and only those. A new performance threshold cleared all 16 data-quality tables, 11 of which (reporting rates, outliers, ratios) are computed without it and came out the same: it now clears five. Choosing a denominator or a maternal denominator cleared the coverage, inequality and health-system tables and the Bayesian models, though the choice is only applied when a table is read: it now clears nothing, and a model fitted for one denominator is still there when you come back to it. Rebuilding afterwards: threshold 0.9 seconds where it took 3 to 7, denominator none where it took 2.2.

  • A new survey year now clears the coverage and inequality tables. They are computed from it, and were left as they were for the year before until something else cleared them.

  • What a dataset keeps is described once (R/cache-tables.R): for each kept table, what it is computed from and how. Its binding, the reactive dependencies it takes and what every setter clears come from that list; the 29 bindings, the clearing cascades and the definitions’ depends_on were three hand-kept copies that disagreed. CacheConnection is 400 lines shorter. What changes for a user:

    • a new first survey year clears the coverage, inequality and Bayesian results (the surveys they are computed from are read from that year on; the results stayed as they were);
    • a new performance threshold, national survey or WUENIC file clears the Bayesian models, which are fitted on the overall score and on the coverage with its surveys;
    • new WUENIC estimates no longer clear the coverage and inequality tables, and new UN mortality estimates no longer clear the mortality summary: neither is computed from them.

  • get_regional_estimates() gives a region’s own rates from the survey files (its latest survey value of each mortality rate and coverage, read through the survey mapping), a district its region’s. A rate the region’s surveys do not give keeps the national value; the national rates are returned whole only when the region is not in the survey files. It read a variable that did not exist.

  • The print headers of the district completeness and outlier tables are shown (their methods were written for classes nothing makes). Documentation regenerated with roxygen2 8.1.0.

  • Fixes from a review of the package:

    • Measles 2 is in the child continuum of care (its column was named measle2).
    • Data Missingness: with a region chosen, the district table showed the whole country.
    • Service utilization: the OPD chart’s “Under-5” and “All ages” lines were labelled the wrong way round.
    • Coverage Target: a dropout indicator is described as a rate below its target, not a coverage above it.
    • plot_comparison_opv1_opv3() is titled and labelled OPV1 and OPV3 (it said Penta1 and Penta3).
    • Twenty error messages are shown. Written cd_abort("x" = ...), they failed with “argument”message” is missing” (a chart’s title, axis or caption that is not one string, a region given for national data, a file that is not a .dta). Three more named a variable where they meant its value.
    • save_dhis2_excel()’s admin sheet, the mortality summary helpers and a district-level filter_service_utilization() used variables that did not exist.
    • The survey estimates leave OPV1 and OPV3 out outside the vaccine group (the test compared values, not names), and the education survey’s levels are ordered.
    • New survey estimates clear the ratios summary, whose expected-ratio row is made from them.

  • One Bayesian fit runs at a time. A fit uses four more R processes for its chains; two fits together took longer than one after the other (about 135 seconds for the pair against 47 each, on 24 cores) and twice the memory. A second fit now waits for the first (options(cd2030.bayes_workers = ) for more).

  • Requires datasuite.ui 0.5.0, where an app starts a page when it is opened.

  • Bayesian Analysis no longer stops the other pages while a fit starts. Handing a fit to its worker sent the worker the environment the request was written in as well as the fit’s inputs: the page’s server, so the dataset, the Shiny session and all they reach. Packing that took the app’s own process minutes (211 seconds, profiled, where the inputs are 0.3 MB), during which the session was busy: no page answered and no chart was sent. The worker is now sent the inputs alone (cd_bayes_fit_task()), which takes no measurable time.

  • Each coverage is defined once (.cd_coverage_defs: what it counts, over which population) and computed on every denominator. It was written out for each of the four (UN, DHIS2, ANC1, Penta1) and each indicator group: 156 lines, now a table. The results are the same to the last digit, at every level, for both groups.

  • A computation uses the indicator group of the dataset it is given, not the one the session last selected (set_selected_group()): with two datasets of different groups open in one session, each is computed with its own indicators. Data that does not say its group is computed with the session’s, as before.

  • New data (set_countdown_data()) clears the adjusted data made from the data before; it is made again from the new data when next read. It was kept, so the coverage that followed was computed from the old data.

  • The dataset’s file is written beside itself and moved into place, so a write cut short (the app closed, the disk full) leaves the file as it was, not half of a new one that cannot be opened.

  • adjustment_values: the yearly numbers as reported and after each step of the dataset’s adjustment are computed once and kept. A report comparing seven indicators ran the whole adjustment seven times (0.8 second each).

  • The table of district outliers can be downloaded. Its button was on the page with nothing behind it and showed as busy for as long as the page was open; a table given no Excel writer now downloads what it shows.

  • The population table (prepare_population_metrics()) prints its header: the method was written for a class nothing makes. Documentation: “admin level 1” has one spelling in words (the column is adminlevel_1), the performance threshold one name, and calculate_overall_score()’s ratio_pairs is described.

  • The check of a class is named after the class: check_cd_data() checks for cd_data, check_cd_equity_data() for cd_equity_data, and so on, one for each class checked in more than one place, all made the same way (.cd_class_check(), in R/utils.R). Five had other names (check_cd_fpet() and check_fpet_data() for the same class, check_equity_data(), check_un_mortality() and check_un_mortality_data(), check_service_utilization()) and 14 places checked such a class by hand. Internal: nothing exported changes.

  • Removed, as nothing called them: check_cd_population_metrics(), check_cd_reporting_rate(), check_scalar_character(), coalesce_join(), extract_un_summary(), calculate_summary() (with aggregate_indicator(), derive_ratio() and threshold_metric(), which only they used), load_public_private(), local_cd_loud() and .rb_note(). None was exported.

  • The functions that take one indicator out of a computed table, ready to plot, are select_*(): select_coverage(), select_inequality(), select_mapping_data(), select_mortality_summary(), select_service_utilization() and select_adjustment_value(). They were filter_*(), which read as filtering rows; they choose an indicator and reshape. The former names still work and say once per session what to call instead (?"cd2030-deprecated"). filter_out_years() and filter_high_performers(), which do filter rows, keep their names, as do the dataset’s methods (cache$filter_mortality_summary(), cache$filter_service_utilization()).

  • The files of the app’s interface are named by what they hold: page-<page id>.R (a page’s part as page-<page id>--<part>.R), filter-, chart-, layout-, wizard- and app-. They were 58 files starting ui-, with two separator styles, the analysis step’s number in the page files and ui-wizard-wizard-*. Nothing in them changed.

  • A dataset’s country is no longer taken for one that only looks like it. The country was the closest name by string distance, so “Sudan” loaded as South Sudan, “Libya” as Liberia, “Mauritius” as Mauritania, “Guyana” as Ghana, “Tonga” as Togo and “Congo Brazzaville” as the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with their UN estimates and surveys, and nothing said so. A name is now matched to a country it names (any of its names in the table, whatever the case, accents or punctuation, or its ISO3 code), to the one country whose name starts with it, or to the one country it is a misspelling of (a letter in a name of five or more, two in nine or more). A misspelling that fits two countries (Nigeria, Niger) is asked about, not guessed. Also found now: “RDC”, “RCA”, “Ivory Coast”, “Republic of Kenya”. A name far from every country gets no suggestion (it got an unrelated one). “Congo” on its own is still the Democratic Republic. Needs stringi.

  • The help pages follow the usual form: a short title in sentence case (147 were in Title Case or were whole sentences), a description of what the function does for its caller, every argument, and what is returned (37 exported functions did not say). Notes on the code’s history that were in the help text are comments in the code. Where the help contradicted the code, the help is corrected: among them the class generate_admin1_service_utilization() returns, plot.cd_overall_score() and two others returning a table, not a plot, compute_service_utilization() taking districts, and get_mapping_data(), which joins coverage to the map and computes none. Four examples called functions that do not exist.

  • save_dhis2_master_data() joined a table that was not defined, so it always failed; it joins the admin sheet. generate_health_system_table()’s error for data that is not national was cut off mid-word.

  • The app’s interface is documented like the rest of the package. Every page, wizard step, filter, chart and table card, layout piece and cd_app() has a help page with what it shows or does, each argument and what it returns, written next to its code and exported there (a _ui / _server pair shares a page); the helpers that are not exported are described the same way in the code. They were 158 names on one page that said to read the source, where 98 of 177 functions had no comment. ?"countdown-pages" stays as the guide, and the site lists them by kind. The same names are exported as before.

  • The table of districts with missing values downloads its rows (its Excel writer wrote a function in their place). A file named with a capital extension (DATA.XLSX) is accepted by the upload box.

  • Guides to get started, as vignettes and on the site: vignette("cd2030.core") (load a dataset, look at its quality, compute coverage, save), vignette("preparing-data") (the workbook, what loading does, why a file does not load), vignette("data-quality"), vignette("coverage") (adjustment, denominators, coverage, reports) and vignette("building-an-app"). Their code runs on the example dataset when the package is built. Needs knitr and rmarkdown to build (Suggests).

  • plot() of an indicator coverage table (calculate_indicator_coverage()) draws again: it failed for every chart type, with “y_vars and legend_labels must have the same length”. The site’s reference index lists get_national_rates() and list_missing_units(), which it left out.

  • Every chart changes its text and its look the same way (?cd_plot_arguments). Each plot() method, the equiplots and plot_comparison() take title, subtitle, caption, x_title, y_title and legend_title, in that order, after the arguments that say what to draw, then chart options by name (background_color, font_family, text_scale, legend_position, …) and options. They had x_axis, x_label or neither for the same thing, legend or legend_title, and many had no subtitle or caption.

  • Breaking: the older names are gone. x_axis and x_label are x_title, y_axis and y_label are y_title, legend and fill_label are legend_title; a chart given an older name stops and names the one to use. The pages, the reports and the apps use the new names. Also renamed, so that one thing has one name:

    • a list of legend entries is legend_labels everywhere, by name, after ...: it was labels on plot() of a coverage table, of a regional coverage table, of the mortality summary, of the completeness of death reporting and of national service utilization, and legend on plot_comparison();
    • the quadrant texts of the preventive against curative chart are quad_labels (was labels), as on the primary health care chart;
    • titles are no longer read from those lists (labels$title, labels$x_axis, labels$y_axis, labels$legend): give title, x_title, y_title, legend_title. The two maps (mortality, service utilization) have no labels argument any more;
    • plot_mortality_plausibility()’s footnote is caption (was note);
    • plot_line_graph() takes x_title and y_title. The three plot_comparison_*() functions write their title and axis titles when none is given (they were default values in the signature). A text held in options wins over the text argument on every chart (it did only on charts with an argument of their own for that text). The three tables drawn by plot() (overall score, utilization data quality, health system) are not charts and are as they were.

  • Charts that did not draw, or drew the wrong text:

    • the trend of completeness for an indicator with every value reported failed (“Faceting variables must have at least one value”): complete indicators were dropped before the one asked for was chosen;
    • a coverage chart (plot() of calculate_indicator_coverage()) draws the indicators the dataset has: the immunization and zero-dose charts failed on an RMNCAH dataset, which has no OPV or IPV;
    • the outlier heat map titled its axes “Year” (under the regions) and “Percent non-outliers” (beside the years), from R and on the Outlier page;
    • the chart of districts with missing values used its vertical title only when a horizontal one was also given, and the other way round.

  • save_data() writes a Stata file for a dataset loaded from a workbook. It failed on raw_month.x, a column the merge of the sheets left behind (with raw_month.y); a loaded dataset no longer has them.

  • calculate_ratios_and_adequacy() is exported: calculate_ratios_summary() takes its result, and could only be used through the dataset object.

  • In the apps:

    • a Stata master file is saved when the wizard is finished. Nothing set in the wizard or after it was ever written for one, and the wizard did not go to edit mode;
    • the Bayesian page has no Custom tab. It offered every indicator, and the model takes only its own, so any other choice was an error;
    • the Custom tab of the coverage, inequality, map and equity cards starts its chart once and follows the choice (serverInput gets a reactive for it; cd_tab_indicator() reads it). It started another chart on the same ids for each choice, and a change to one chart’s options was also written for the indicators chosen before;
    • a table card with a year control downloads the year shown, as its file’s name and its sheet’s title say. It held every year;
    • the Sub-National Inequality card has its own title (it read “National Inequality”);
    • the consistency check no longer starts a second ratios chart that is on no page (the AI was told of it).

  • filter_high_performers() (the table of units meeting a target) keeps units below the threshold for a dropout indicator, as the chart counts them. It kept those at or above it.

  • Every help page has examples (187 had none). Those that can run from the example dataset do, and are run when the package is checked; the Shiny pieces show how they are used in a page.

  • The private sector chart (plot() of prepare_private_sector_plot_data()) takes its texts as the other charts do: legend_labels (public, private), indicator_labels, area_labels and share_label in place of one labels list.

  • Loading:

    • load_data() and load_excel_parts() with a start_year load the data from that year on. Any start_year stopped the load (“‘length = …’ in coercion to ‘logical(1)’”);
    • a Stata file is read with its months as an ordered factor of the month names, as a workbook is. A file written by save_data() could not be read back (“Can’t join x$month with y$month”), nor one with months as labelled values;
    • load_private_sector_data() and load_csection_estimates() keep the rows of country_iso when the data holds several countries (the argument was not read).

  • The Bayesian model fits institutional deliveries ("ideliv") on data that names them instdeliveries or instlivebirths, as the built-in surveys and the coverage tables do. That tab stopped with “object ‘r_ideliv’ not found”.

  • plot() of the health system comparison draws its default chart, delivery coverage against workforce density (the comparison did not carry cov_instdeliveries_*).

  • plot() of the overall score table and of the utilization data quality table shows every year when years is not given (it stopped with “years cannot be null”).

  • Smaller: adjustment_settings_footnote() takes labels for some of the groups or indicators (a partial named vector stopped it); get_national_rates() returns its table visibly; cd_bayes_install_command() returns nothing when nothing is missing (it gave install.packages(c(""), ...)); the FPET text says “decreased by 0.005”, not “decreased by -0.005 points”; a report’s list of regions has each region once.

  • Institutional deliveries have a coverage: cov_ideliv_*, the deliveries in facilities over the deliveries. There was none, so every chart, map and report asking for the coverage of ideliv was drawn empty (“Column cov_ideliv_anc1 not found”): the column that existed is cov_instdeliveries_*, which is the live births in facilities over the deliveries (Stata’s column). It is kept, and labelled for what it is (“Institutional Live Births per Delivery”).

  • Charts name indicators by their labels, not their codes. The heat maps of missing values and of outliers showed anc_1trimester, bcg, instlivebirths…; the continuum heat map showed anc1 for an indicator its caller had not listed. cd_indicator_labels() gives the labels (translated with a translator), the two heat maps take indicator_labels, and the pages and reports give them the app’s language.

  • The heat maps read better: softer red, amber and green, numbers that stay readable on each colour and get smaller as the columns get many, axes titled for what they hold (“Indicator”, “Admin level 1”), and on the continuum heat map each tile’s value and the indicators’ names level and wrapped.

  • The PHC performance chart draws its quadrants as the preventive against curative chart does: a text in each corner (it was placed at half and one and a half times the median, over the points), dashed median lines, and a faint tint on the quadrant high on both axes and on the one low on both.

cd2030.core 1.3.10

  • Bayesian Analysis no longer holds the app up. The fit already ran in another R process, but its result did not: a fitted model carried the sampler’s draws and the compiled Stan model (13 MB national, 41 MB sub-national), which were brought back from the worker, kept in the dataset and written to its file, taking 3 to 6 seconds when a fit ended and again, for every model kept, each time anything else in the dataset changed. generate_bayes_model() now returns the model without them (keep_samples = FALSE: about 30 KB and 170 KB), the charts and bayes_model_estimates() being drawn from the summary it keeps, pixel for pixel as before. Models already saved in a dataset are held without their draws when it is opened, and written so at its next save (slim_bayes_model()).

  • Requires datasuite.ui 0.4.4 (the Ask AI button’s hint is its text, not the markup around it).

  • Maps: choosing years one after another no longer sets the maps redrawing without end. Each choice was sent back to the years chip, and arrived after the next click, undoing it; the two selections then replaced each other for good (cd_years_sync(), on every page with a years chip).

  • Charts in reports are drawn without tick marks on their axes, as the charts on the pages are (cd_report_theme()). A chart’s Tick marks option still draws them for that chart.

  • Reports take the app’s colour: the Countdown report theme (accent and headings) is the vaccine app’s blue in the vaccine app, as its pages are, where every app’s reports were the RMNCAH maroon (cd_app(theme = )). A report saved before keeps the colours saved with it; choosing the Countdown theme again in its Design gives it the app’s.

cd2030.core 1.3.9

  • Load Data: the required columns are checked at the Data Quality step, not only at Finish. new_countdown()’s check (check_required_columns_exist()) now also covers the population columns (Total_Population, Population_under_5years, Population_under_1year, Live_births, Total_births, Women_15_49_years, Pop_growth_rate) besides the group’s indicators and reporting rates, and the wizard asks the same question of the unmerged sheets (check_required_columns_presheet()), naming what is missing by sheet, as the workbook spells it. A workbook without Pop_growth_rate used to pass every check and fail at Finish with “false must be a vector, not NULL” in the first district.
  • Load Data: every data quality issue can be downloaded as an Excel workbook from the Data Quality step: a summary of the checks and one row per issue, with nothing shortened (quality_issues_table(), write_quality_issues()).
  • Bayesian model, sub-national: it is fitted. generate_bayes_model() stopped with “Column source doesn’t exist” for every indicator: the regional coverage had the survey’s source as source.x beside the admin mapping’s own source (source.y), because the mapping was joined whole. Only its two names are joined now (calculate_coverage() and calculate_indicator_coverage() at admin level 1), so regional coverage has source again and no admin1_key.
  • The Bayesian models’ estimates as tables: bayes_model_estimates() (coverage by year, 2010 to 2030, in percent, with the 95% and 80% intervals; a row per region for a sub-national model) and a dataset’s $bayes_estimates(admin_level), every model already fitted at a level in one table.
  • The Bayesian Analysis pages are here (bayesian_ui(), bayesian_page_server(), moved from cd2030.rmncah), for every app: their tabs are cd_cfg("bayes_indicators") (default cd_bayes_indicators). future and promises are imported for them.

cd2030.core 1.3.8

  • calculate_indicator_coverage(): zero-dose and under-vaccinated coverage were wrong by a factor of about a million (the population in thousands was multiplied by 1000 instead of divided: (pop*1000 - penta1)/pop*1000), and for the ANC1-, Penta1- and derived denominators, which are counts, the 1000 did not belong at all. They are now the share of surviving infants without penta1 (zero-dose) or penta3 (under-vaccinated), as in the Countdown 2030 Stata code.
  • Measles2 coverage is divided by the infants surviving to the second dose (totmeasles2_*), as in the Stata code and as the derived denominators already did, not by those surviving to the first.
  • Notebook data: a dataset’s notebooks get every table the CacheConnection has (51: the data, the results each page shows, the reference data), each listed with what it holds (ds_list()’s new description, and the list DataSuite shows in Stata’s dslist). notebook_data("prepare", tables = ) writes only the tables asked for, so Stata notebooks get a table when a cell first uses it; Python’s are the usual twelve, as before. wealth_survey is the wealth-quintile survey again (it read a member that does not exist, so it was always empty).
  • notebook_data("describe"): the notebook’s dataset’s tables with their columns and what each column holds (cd_describe_columns()), its grain and key columns, read from the .rds without changing it. DataSuite gives it to its assistant when it writes a notebook’s code, and shows it when you hover a table or a column in a notebook.
  • In R notebooks, the attached data (datasuite:data) names its tables in the attribute jovian.tables, so the kernel’s variables pane and data viewer list and show them without reading the others or the ds_* functions.
  • Requires datasuite.ui 0.4.3: charts and tables already drawn follow a change of language.
  • STATA-DIFFERENCES.md lists where the package and the Countdown 2030 Stata code still differ, by choice.

cd2030.core 1.3.7

  • cd_table_card_ui() / cd_table_card_server(): a flextable in a chart card, with its picture and its data (Excel) in the card’s header; the screen and the picture are drawn by the same function. The Overall Score page uses it (and rmncah’s Service Utilization data quality and national Health System pages). DataSuite’s AI can read the table.
  • cd_upload_data_ui() / cd_upload_data_server(): the Load Data screen the apps had each kept a copy of; cd_app() uses it unless the app passes its own. An app describes its part of the wizard with options(cd2030.wizard = ...) as before.
  • cd_minimal_theme(): ggplot2::theme_minimal() with a choice of grid lines (the subnational coverage dot plot and heat map, and cd2030.pooled’s charts). The colours several charts share (the traffic-light categories, the year colours, Data Adjustment’s steps…) and the theme pieces they repeated (the dashed grid, the maps’ theme) are defined once (R/utils-plot-themes.R); the charts look as before.
  • A failed reference-data upload (UN, WUENIC or UN mortality estimates) says why in its banner, instead of “Unsupported file format” for every error, and no longer prints the error to the console.
  • sf is used through sf:: instead of imported, so loading cd2030.core no longer loads sf (and GDAL, GEOS and PROJ) until a map is drawn or a shapefile read. officer is no longer imported whole (officer::fp_border() is its only use). No longer imports janitor, which nothing used.
  • Needs datasuite.ui 0.4.2: inside DataSuite, cd_request_bayes_packages() asks it to install the Bayesian model’s packages through datasuite.ui::ds_host_request().

cd2030.core 1.3.6

  • notebook_data(): a folder’s Countdown datasets for DataSuite’s notebooks (an app’s notebookData) – by name in R, and as Stata files for Python and Stata notebooks, made again when their .rds changes.
  • The Bayesian model’s packages are installed when it is first wanted: cd_bayes_packages_missing() (checked without loading Stan), cd_request_bayes_packages() (inside DataSuite, asks it to install them) and cd_bayes_install_command() (the install.packages() call, for plain R). DESCRIPTION’s Config/datasuite/onDemand keeps DataSuite’s background install from fetching them; R itself ignores it.
  • No longer suggests chromote, countrycode, png, ragg, rsvg, svglite or systemfonts, which nothing used.

cd2030.core 1.3.5

  • Data Adjustment is one page for the data kept and how it is corrected (the Remove Years page is gone; its years are the page’s first section):
    • Remove years everywhere, or a region’s or district’s data for some or every year.
    • Completeness by each indicator group’s k or an indicator’s own, outliers and missing values – each can be switched off everywhere or for a region or district, with its own k; a district’s rules come before its region’s, a region’s before everywhere’s.
    • Beside each setting, what the check pages found (reporting rates, districts below the threshold, outliers and missing values by indicator: adjustment_evidence()).
    • The settings are saved in the dataset (cache$adjustment_settings, cache$set_adjustment_settings()); a dataset saved before reads its k-factors and removed years as settings (adjustment_settings_from_k()).
    • New: adjustment_settings_default(), adjustment_settings_check(), adjustment_settings_footnote() (the rules in a sentence each, for reports) and adjustment_steps_used(); adjust_service_data() and generate_adjustment_values() take settings (and the latter an area and level).
  • Data Adjustment Changes shows, for each year, the reported count beside the adjusted count made of its parts (completeness, missing values, the outliers’ correction; a correction that lowers the count drawn as removed), with the same in a table – a step an indicator does not get reads “Off” – for every area, a region or a district, and the rules in force. The adjustment report chart is the same.
  • Tables show a table’s loader while they are computed.
  • Bayesian models: bayes_model_key(), bayes_model_cached(), bayes_model_inputs() and keep_bayes_model(), so an app can fit a model in the background and keep it.
  • Requires datasuite.ui 0.4.0 (reports written by Quire’s writers).

cd2030.core 1.3.4

  • The AI can read and change a saved report instead of replacing it: new AI bridge actions (datasuite.ui 0.3.4’s report_list(), report_read() and report_update_blocks()):
    • listReports (read): the reports saved in the dataset.
    • readReport (read): a report’s blocks in order – the text of its headings, paragraphs and notes, and for each chart and table its kind, settings, options and a short table of the data it shows – and its language.
    • updateBlocks (replace): targeted changes by block id – write or rewrite text, change a chart’s kind, settings, chart options or layout, insert blocks after one, remove or move blocks – checked as a whole and saved once, with the report’s id kept; everything else in the report stays as it is. The user’s permission setting may ask them first, with a summary such as Write 5 paragraphs in the report "Benin National Coverage" (benin.rds) or each change (Chart "Coverage trend" (anc4): Coverage trend -> Coverage map; year none -> 2023). The Reports page shows the change at once, the open report too.
  • A report the AI saves (saveReport) carries its own id, as the builder’s reports do: the Reports page saves edits by it, so edits to a report the AI had saved were not saved (datasuite.ui 0.3.4 also repairs the reports saved before).
  • Needs datasuite.ui 0.3.4; every package in Imports has a minimum version.

cd2030.core 1.3.3

  • CacheConnection$denominator_comparison(indicator, admin_level, region): the Denominator Selection comparison as one tidy table – for each indicator and year, its coverage under each denominator option (id and label) next to the survey estimate of that year with its bounds, the difference in percentage points, and which denominator is the one chosen for the indicator. The same numbers as the Denominator Selection charts (calculate_derived_coverage()), one row per denominator, so the Countdown AI can compare the options in one call. By default it compares the indicators the page does. It is chartable, defined in cache_definition(), and its new columns (denominator_label, selected, coverage, survey, survey_lower, survey_upper, difference, survey_year) are in the data dictionary.

cd2030.core 1.3.2

  • Portuguese: the translations and the report presets’ questions read as Portuguese is written in Mozambique and Angola (European norm) instead of Brazilian Portuguese (“Contagem decrescente para 2030”, “nados vivos”, “Dados em falta”, “Transferir”…).

cd2030.core 1.3.1

  • A data dictionary: cd_dictionary() says what the ids and column names in the package’s data mean – the six denominator options (id, label, what it is, levels), indicators, target populations, reporting rates, fixed columns and how names are built (cov_<indicator>_<denominator>, <population>_<denominator>, r_<indicator>, …). cd_describe_columns() reads column names with it (“Coverage of Pentavalent 3 (%), denominator: Penta1 population growth (penta1derived)”) and never guesses a name it can’t read. cd_denominator_labels() gives the labels, translated when given a translator.
  • The denominators have one set of labels everywhere – UN projections, DHIS2 projections, ANC1-derived, Penta1-derived, ANC1 population growth, Penta1 population growth – in the denominator chip, the Denominator Selection charts, the reports and the plot legends (new translation keys lbl_denom_anc1_growth and lbl_denom_penta1_growth). anc1/penta1 are the -derived options and anc1derived/penta1derived the population-growth ones; the ids are unchanged.
  • inst/scripts/export-data-dictionary.R writes the docs’ “Data dictionary” reference page from it.
  • Every public member of CacheConnection is defined (R/cache-definitions.R): cache_definition() says what each data point is in the methodology’s terms – its kind (data, setting, reference, mapping, check, value, store, state, method, action), its grain (what one row is) and key columns, its unit, where the user sets it in the app and which pages show it, the methodology docs section it comes from, the defaults it follows (ids of cd_methodology_defaults()) and the members it is computed from. Columns are left to the data dictionary. cache_manifest() includes each member’s definition. A test fails when a member is added without one, or when a docs link or default reference doesn’t resolve. Eight members are marked draft with a note (among them get_regional_estimates(), which fails for a region because it reads an undefined object).
  • inst/scripts/export-cache-reference.R writes the docs’ “CacheConnection reference” page from the definitions.

cd2030.core 1.3.0

The constants of the Countdown methodology are defined once, in R/methodology-defaults.R:

  • cd_methodology_defaults() lists them (the adjustment’s k and reporting-rate cutoff, the 5 x MAD outlier rule, the district reporting threshold, the ratio ranges and score components, the default rates of the denominators, the coverage targets, the mortality flags), each with its step, indicator group, unit, label, note and source file. The functions that use them read them from there, so the documented values are the ones the code runs with.
  • inst/scripts/export-methodology-defaults.R writes them as the JSON the DataSuite docs read; the AI guide sync workflow also regenerates it on each release and opens a pull request on the docs.

The AI bridge actions:

  • setFilters only changes the view; saveReport and addGraph add, or replace when the id given is already saved; generateReport adds a file, or replaces one of the same name. Each describes itself for the user’s confirmation, which DataSuite asks only before a replacement.
  • A report’s image block that names a figure the AI saved in the dataset’s analysis folder is stored in the dataset as a picture, so the report keeps it (PNG or JPEG from that folder only, up to 5 MB).
  • Generated reports go in the analysis folder’s reports/.
  • Requires datasuite.ui 0.3.0.

cd2030.core 1.2.0

For the Countdown AI in DataSuite (countdown-analytics/docs/AI-PLAN.md), everything around CacheConnection:

  • The MCP server (cd2030_mcp_server() and its tools) is removed; the AI works from CacheConnection itself.
  • cache_manifest(): every public member of CacheConnection with its arguments (defaults, allowed values), its documentation and whether it writes or can be charted, plus the report kinds, read from the installed package.
  • CacheConnection$decompose_change(): which districts (or regions) drive a change in an indicator’s coverage between two years, split into service delivery and denominator, with a reporting-rate flag.
  • CacheConnection$revision goes up with every saved change; init_CacheConnection(read_only = TRUE) opens a dataset without ever writing it (the AI’s copy).
  • Custom charts: report kind custom_chart (data from a CacheConnection member, fixed transforms, a plot description; never code), cd_chartable_members(), cd_member_data(), cd_custom_chart_data(), and saved graphs in the dataset (set_graph(), graphs), which reports can use.
  • The AI bridge: the Countdown pages’ charts and tables say which report kind they are and with which options; the state has the dataset’s path, country and revision; new actions saveReport, addGraph and generateReport.
  • Requires datasuite.ui 0.2.0.

cd2030.core 1.1.1

Documentation only; no change to the code.

  • A new README: what the package does, where it fits (DataSuite, the Countdown apps, datasuite.ui), installing from r-universe, a walkthrough on the bundled Kenya data, CacheConnection, indicator groups, reports, building an app with cd_app(), developing and releasing.
  • ?cd2030.core and ?countdown-pages give overviews of the entry points and the Countdown pages.
  • The pkgdown reference index lists every help topic; URL and BugReports point to github.com/damurka/cd2030.core.
  • The Bayesian coverage packages come from https://alkemalab.r-universe.dev (Additional_repositories).

cd2030.core 1.1.0

  • Report builder: standard reports rebuilt as blocks (report_presets()), exported to Word, PowerPoint and PDF through datasuite.ui’s report engine; cd_report_context() is a dataset’s report context.
  • The Countdown pages every Countdown app shares (data quality, denominators, coverage, equity, the Load Data wizard, filters, nav sections and cd_app()) moved here from the apps, built on datasuite.ui.
  • Chart options (cd_chart_options() and friends) and the report engine now live in datasuite.ui; they are imported and re-exported here, so existing code keeps working.
  • Countdown’s translations (indicator names, chart titles, page texts) are in inst/translation/cd2030.json.

cd2030.core 1.0.0

  • Initial Release
  • CacheConnection now names a file-backed cache after its source file’s basename (<stem>.rds) instead of <country>_<timestamp>.rds, and loads an existing matching cache directly instead of treating a fresh parse as authoritative when one is already present – this decision now lives entirely in CacheConnection itself, so it applies uniformly regardless of caller.
  • Added cd2030_mcp_server(), an optional (mcptools/ellmer Suggests) Model Context Protocol server exposing read-only tools – data quality, coverage, inequality, mortality, service utilization, health system, and private-sector queries, plus report generation and coverage charts – over an already-processed .rds cache, for use with LLM clients like Claude Desktop or Claude Code.
  • Expanded the MCP server from 12 to 38 tools, covering every remaining read-only CacheConnection method (mutating setters and non-data methods remain deliberately unreachable).
  • Standardized MCP tool naming/documentation against the CD2030 analytical framework’s own vocabulary (get_coverage_targets, get_continuum_of_care renamed to match; DQA/mortality/health-system tool descriptions now cite the framework’s official metric IDs and named indices), and added the three “Equity Assessment” equiplot tools (get_equiplot_area, get_equiplot_wealth, get_equiplot_education), bringing the total to 41.
  • Fixed stray print() debug statements in generate_report(), generate_coverage_data(), and generate_bayes_model() that corrupted the MCP server’s stdio JSON-RPC stream (stdout doubles as the wire protocol, so any incidental console output there breaks every client response).
  • MCP tool results are now also capped by total cell count (max_cells, default 5000), not just row count: a row-only cap doesn’t protect against a very wide table (e.g. get_indicator_coverage at district level, ~190 columns), where even a handful of rows produced a megabyte-scale response that crashed a live client connection.
  • Six MCP tools (get_overall_score, get_inequality, get_completeness_summary, get_outliers_summary, get_reporting_rate, get_service_utilization_summary) now read CacheConnection’s cached active bindings (e.g. reporting_rate_district) instead of always calling the always-recomputing calculate_*/compute_* method, whenever no region filter is requested – the exact case those bindings cover. Verified identical output to a direct recompute for all six.
